title: Semester and Group Chat
premise: Wendell Halloran has built her whole life on being unreadable — until the ghost haunting Marrow Creek High starts leaving her handwritten notes that know her real name, her dead mother's nickname, and secrets Wendell never told anyone. The notes lead her to a hidden archive proving the school's beloved founder stole his fortune and his ideas from a silenced Black student, whose descendant is a classmate Wendell has quietly betrayed for social safety. As the ghost's ink begins to fade — and with it, apparently, Wendell's own memories of her mother — she must expose the truth publicly, at the cost of her best friend's family legacy and her own carefully constructed invisibility. In the end, Wendell chooses testimony over anonymity: the archive goes public, the friendship fractures but slowly mends, and the ghost's final note reveals it was never a ghost at all, but memory itself demanding a witness.
about_author: Isandro Fairweather is the pen name of a former night-shift school custodian who spent years reading the marginalia students left behind in desks and library books. They write young adult fiction about quiet kids who discover that silence is also a kind of story.

chapters.title: Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Wendell's POV. We meet Wendell through her rules of invisibility: head down, grades up, no posts under her real name. Her anonymous coding account, @nullhalloran, is popular precisely because no one knows it's her. Emotional beat: the comfort and loneliness of being unreadable.

chapters.title: The First Note
chapters.summary: Wendell finds a note in her locker addressed 'Dear Wendell' — not Wendy, not Halloran — in ink that shimmers wrong under fluorescent light. It references her mother's private pet name for her, which appears nowhere online. Beat: fear sharpening into fascination.

chapters.title: Marrow Creek's Famous Ghost
chapters.summary: Best friend Priya Chandra recounts the school legend of the Founder's Ghost, a story every class inherits. Wendell realizes the notes match the legend's details exactly. She lies to Priya about why she's asking. Beat: the first hairline crack in the friendship.

chapters.title: Impossible Ink
chapters.summary: Wendell tests the second note chemically in chemistry class; the ink has no known composition and rewrites itself overnight. Her anonymous account starts receiving messages from someone who knows her handle AND her face. Beat: paranoia — the two halves of her life are colliding.

chapters.title: What My Mother Left Me
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter to Wendell's mother's death two years ago and the half-finished notebook she left behind, full of local history research. The ghost's notes quote it verbatim. Beat: grief reopened; Wendell wants answers more than safety now.

chapters.title: The Archive Under the Auditorium
chapters.summary: Following the third note's clues, Wendell finds a sealed crawlspace behind the auditorium containing boxes of founding-era documents — including letters signed by a student named Ezekiel Okafor, erased from every plaque. Beat: awe curdling into anger.

chapters.title: Founder's Luck
chapters.summary: Research chapter: founder Ambrose Marrow's celebrated 'inventions' and donated fortune are traced, page by page, to Ezekiel's confiscated work. Priya's family name appears among the early benefactors. Beat: dread — telling this truth will hurt people Wendell loves.

chapters.title: Priya Knows Something
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She's found her grandmother's old letters referencing an 'arrangement' with the Marrow estate and suspects Wendell is hiding something too. The girls circle each other at lunch, both lying warmly. Beat: dramatic irony and mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: The Account That Knew Too Much
chapters.summary: @nullhalloran receives a direct message: 'You found the boxes. Now they'll find you.' Wendell discovers the school administration has been quietly monitoring student accounts — hers included. Beat: surveillance horror; power watching back.

chapters.title: Vice-Principal Voss
chapters.summary: Wendell is summoned and offered a quiet deal: return whatever she took from the crawlspace, keep her scholarship clean, forget Ezekiel Okafor. Voss quotes her mother's notebook back at her. Beat: cold institutional menace; the corruption has faces.

chapters.title: Ink Fading
chapters.summary: The notes begin to fade physically, and Wendell notices her memories of her mother blurring in parallel — her voice, the nickname, gone soft at the edges. The ghost warns: 'Memory needs a witness or it dies.' Beat: ticking clock established.

chapters.title: Ezekiel's Descendant
chapters.summary: Wendell tracks Ezekiel's living descendant: Marcus Okafor, the quiet senior she once threw under the bus socially to protect her reputation. She must confess what she did to ask for his trust. Beat: shame faced head-on; the cost of invisibility made personal.

chapters.title: Confession in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. He already knew about the notes; his family kept their own copy of Ezekiel's letters for generations. He forgives Wendell conditionally: help restore the record, or stay out of his way. Beat: uneasy alliance, earned not given.

chapters.title: The Centennial Gala
chapters.summary: The school announces its centennial gala celebrating Ambrose Marrow — the perfect stage and the perfect deadline. Wendell, Priya, and Marcus plan to replace the ceremony program with the true history. Beat: heist energy, rising hope.

chapters.title: Priya's Choice
chapters.summary: Priya confronts Wendell: she found the plan and her grandmother's complicity with it. Torn between family honor and truth, she walks out — then secretly photographs the original letters as insurance. Beat: heartbreak with a hidden hinge of loyalty.

chapters.title: Locked Doors
chapters.summary: The night before the gala, the crawlspace is emptied and Wendell's locker is padlocked by administration. Voss suspends her pending 'investigation.' The ghost's penultimate note appears anyway — on Wendell's skin, faint as a scar. Beat: darkest hour.

chapters.title: Everything Priya Kept
chapters.summary: Priya arrives at Wendell's door with her grandmother's letters and the photographs: proof enough to rebuild the case even without the archive. The friends reconcile not with apology alone but with shared work through the night. Beat: repair; love as evidence.

chapters.title: The Gala
chapters.summary: Climax part one. During the founder's tribute, the AV system — Wendell's code — overrides the slideshow with Ezekiel's letters, her mother's voice on tape, and the fading ink notes projected huge. The room erupts; Voss moves to cut power. Beat: triumphant chaos.

chapters.title: Witness
chapters.summary: Climax part two. Wendell takes the microphone and testifies — naming Ezekiel, naming her own betrayals, naming her mother. Marcus stands beside her; students hold up phone lights. The board can't silence three hundred witnesses. Beat: courage as public act.

chapters.title: The Last Note
chapters.summary: The morning after, the final note appears, fully legible one last time: it was never a ghost — it was the accumulated refusal of everyone erased, waiting for someone to read aloud. The ink dissolves into blank paper. Beat: mystery resolved as meaning, not mechanics.

chapters.title: Renaming
chapters.summary: Fallout and change: the school votes to rename the library for Ezekiel Okafor; Voss resigns; Wendell's suspension is reversed. She posts about her mother openly under her real name for the first time. Beat: grief integrated; inheritance reclaimed.

chapters.title: Head Up
chapters.summary: Epilogue, spring semester. Wendell archives @nullhalloran and starts a new account under her own name. Priya and Marcus help unveil the plaque; Wendell leaves a fresh note in a random locker for whoever needs it next. Beat: visibility chosen freely; the cycle turned generous.
